findings.rootCause: LeoRolloutProfile.parse returned the caller's fallback (SAFE_CARDINALITY_CORRECTION from fromSystemProperties) for ANY non-blank value that was not an exact enum/external name, so 'disabled', 'false', 'off', 'none', '0' and typos silently enabled learned cardinality correction at the LMDB consumer (LmdbOperatorFeedbackStats.rollout()). The enum constructor discarded explainEnabled/ruleSteeringEnabled, so OBSERVE_ONLY == SHADOW_EXPLAIN observably and SAFE_RULE_STEERING/SAFE_PLAN_RERANKING (lifecycle=false) sat above SAFE_PLAN_LIFECYCLE (lifecycle=true): the declared order was not a ladder. Adjacent: LeoEvidence.bestOf ranked Kind before any trust, so a 0-confidence/0-sample QUERY_LOCAL_VIRTUAL_SKETCH outranked a 200-sample 0.95-confidence SCALAR_OPERATOR_FEEDBACK.
findings.change: LeoRolloutProfile.parse fails closed: blank/null -> fallback (unconfigured default unchanged); known enum name or externalName (case-insensitive, '-'/'_' interchangeable, trimmed) -> that profile; explicit negative aliases off/disabled/false/none/0 -> OFF silently; every other value -> OFF with a once-per-distinct-value WARN naming the accepted values (bounded set, so the per-estimate re-evaluation in rollout() cannot log-spam - critique 3.7.4 minor). explainEnabled/ruleSteeringEnabled are retained as fields with accessors and the two experimental rungs now also enforce plan lifecycle, making the declared order a monotone superset ladder (design's preferred option). LeoEvidence.bestOf keeps Kind precedence among candidates that carry trust (protected, or confidence>0 && evidenceCount>0) and only falls back to untrusted candidates when nothing trusted exists (never empty for a non-empty finite input). Sound because: fail-closed is the roadmap 4.5 rule for configuration, the fallback is reserved for the genuinely unconfigured case, and kind precedence among trusted candidates keeps LeoEvidenceTest#evidencePriorityPrefersQueryLocalSketchOverScalarCorrection (sketch confidence 0.75) green.

findings.rootCause: LeoConfidenceModel: (i) correctionRatio/qError mapped non-finite or negative inputs to 1.0 and observe had no validity check, so a NaN sample counted, pulled the EWMA toward 1 (erasing a learned 100x correction) and raised base confidence; (ii) EWMA_ALPHA=0.6 in LINEAR ratio space made alternating 100x under/over estimates settle in a 71/29 oscillation instead of the geometric mean 1; (iii) clamp(actual / max(1, estimate)) floored only the estimate, so one empty execution yielded MIN_CORRECTION_RATIO=1e-6 (50 rows -> 5e-5); (iv) rowQErrorMax never decayed and the confidence penalty used it plus a cumulative linear coefficient of variation, so one 1e5 outlier pinned confidence at 0 despite 50 accurate samples; (v) decayedConfidence returned the undecayed value when currentEpoch <= lastEpoch and observe stored max(lastEpoch, epoch), so after an epoch-counter regression stale evidence never decayed.
findings.change: Regression-safe learning (roadmap 4.5) inside the immutable value class, public accessors preserved: (i) observe returns `this` when any input is non-finite or negative (no count, no ratio move, no epoch refresh); (ii) corrections are learned as a geometric (log-space) EWMA with the same alpha 0.6 (first sample stores the raw ratio bit-exactly); (iii) correctionRatio = clamp(max(actual,1) / max(estimate,1)) - an empty result can never correct below one row; (iv) a per-sample decayed q-error statistic (Q_ERROR_DECAY 0.85, floored at 1) drives the penalty while rowQErrorMax/workQErrorMax stay the true historical maxima for diagnostics/uncertainty bounds, and the cumulative linear CoV is replaced by an EWMA variance of ln(ratio) around the log-space correction (variancePenalty = min(0.85, 0.5*sigma_log/ln 10)); (v) decayedConfidence uses |currentEpoch - lastEpoch| and observe re-anchors lastEpoch = epoch. fromPersisted sanitizes every field (ratios clamped, decayed <= max, variance >= 0, non-finite confidence recomputed). Persistence: the two decayed q-errors and the log-variance replace rowRatioMean/rowRatioM2 in LearnedOperatorCounts/LearnedMultiplierCounts (LmdbOperatorFeedbackStats) and FanoutAccumulator (LmdbLeoSurfaceStats); PERSIST_VERSION 23->24 and LmdbLeoFeedbackStore.VERSION 6->7 so polluted sidecars are dropped once (design's recommended option; version assertions in four LMDB tests updated accordingly). Existing LeoConfidenceModelTest calibrations (stable(3)=0.50, stable(8)=0.875, highVariance keeps rowQErrorMax>=100, recentSamples exp(0.6 ln 10)=3.98>3, zeroEstimate->0) hold, as verified by the green module run. Critique 3.7.3 minor (LMDB wrappers still count NaN-planned samples): after reading the code, observationFor(...) already falls back to costFeedbackExpectedRows/resultSizeEstimate/actualRows so planned values are finite at the wrapper; the wrapper's sums are execution-derived (actual/left/right rows) and valid without a prediction, while recordRowQError/recordWorkQError and the model skip invalid planned values - this decision is now documented in LearnedOperatorCounts.add/LearnedMultiplierCounts.add (doc-only change). Design deviation: the design suggested making correctionBlendConfidence read decayed q-errors to avoid a 'forever cap'; the code shows it uses the q-error maximum as a bounded confidence BOOST guarded by a coherence check, not a cap, so no change was made there.

Behaviour change of an existing setting: rdf4j.optimizer.lmdb.leo.rolloutProfile / rdf4j.optimizer.lmdb.leoProfile / rdf4j.optimizer.lmdb.leo.profile now fail closed - any non-blank value that is not a known profile name resolves to OFF (off/disabled/false/none/0 silently; anything else with a one-time WARN listing accepted values). SAFE_RULE_STEERING and SAFE_PLAN_RERANKING now also enforce plan lifecycle (monotone ladder). Sidecar formats bumped: LmdbOperatorFeedbackStats PERSIST_VERSION 23->24, LmdbLeoFeedbackStore VERSION 6->7 (old sidecars are dropped and relearned once).
crossWpNotes: The PERSIST_VERSION 23->24 bump also discards the persisted FrontierLearningModel serialized in the same .operators sidecar (wp5 owns frontier lifecycle) - one-time relearn; coordinate so the bump happens once if wp5 also changes the format.

Harness impact (critique 3.7.4 minor): scripts/leo-workload-template.txt and scripts/leo-workload-benchmark.sh run profiles safe_rule_steering / safe_plan_reranking, which now also enforce plan lifecycle; benchmark trajectories under those two profiles may shift.

A misspelled profile now yields OFF and LmdbSailStore may skip learned-service initialisation entirely (sidecars not loaded) where it previously silently ran SAFE_CARDINALITY_CORRECTION - intended fail-closed behaviour, logged once.

3.7.3 observation: LmdbOperatorFeedbackStats.observationFor falls back to plannedRows := actualRows when neither the contract, costFeedbackExpectedRows nor resultSizeEstimate is finite, which records a no-prediction execution as a perfect (q-error 1, ratio 1) sample at the LMDB layer - the same defect class one layer above the model. Not changed here (dropping it would also drop valid execution-derived wrapper sums; needs a NaN-tolerant plannedRowsSum). Flagged as follow-up for the 3.7.1/3.7.5 batches that own the publication path.

Critique's cross-sidecar epoch note: LmdbLeoSurfaceStats surfaces use confidenceModel.confidence() directly (never decayedConfidence), so the epoch-distance decay fix does not change surface trust; only decayForMutation applies. No change needed for this batch; the suggested recordStoreMutation post-condition assertion belongs to the 3.7.5 batch.
followUps: Decide whether observationFor's last-resort plannedRows := actualRows fallback should leave plannedRows NaN (with NaN-tolerant plannedRowsSum / reconstructedConfidenceModel) so no-prediction executions stop counting as perfect samples at the LMDB layer.

Optional: an LMDB-level test that a no-prediction observation does not raise learned-multiplier confidence (design 'additionalTests') was not added because plannedRows cannot be NaN at the wrapper today (see above).
Re-run PackedFrontierSubsetKernelContractTest on an idle host to close the flaky-timeout triage with a green (two timeouts observed at load average 82-111; passed at 23:08 on identical code).
